title: Public speaking, rhetoric and oral advocacy
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Plan, write and deliver informative and persuasive speeches, use classical rhetoric (ethos, pathos and logos), handle questions, and practice the basics of oral argument and debate.
primary_reading: Stand up, Speak out (University of Minnesota Libraries open textbook)

weeks.7: Classical rhetoric: ethos, pathos and logos

blocks.deliverable: Analyze the audience for a 3-minute talk.
Outline a speech with an introduction, three points and a conclusion.
Record a 3-minute speech and critique your delivery.
Week 7 midterm; write a persuasive speech using Monroe's motivated sequence.
Prepare answers to five hostile questions about your speech.
Deliver a 5-minute argument on a supplied problem and answer questions.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Moot argument: using a short case file supplied in the project, prepare and record (or deliver to a listener) a 10-minute argument for one side, with a written outline and a list of anticipated questions and answers.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
